title: Reconstructing a quasi-coherent sheaf on standard Proj from all twisted sections
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}S_d$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring generated over $S_0$ by finitely many elements of $S_1$, and put $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $\mathcal F(n)=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(n)$ for $n\in\mathbf Z$, where $\mathcal O_X(n)=\widetilde{S(n)}$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Equip $N=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\Gamma(X,\mathcal F(n))$ with its graded $S$-module action: for $s\in S_e$ and $t\in N_n$, multiply the canonical section $s$ of $\mathcal O_X(e)$ with $t$ via the multiplication maps of [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor], obtaining $st\in N_{n+e}$. There is a canonical isomorphism $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}:\widetilde N\longrightarrow\mathcal F$. On $D_+(f)$ for $f\in S_1$ its map on sections is $N_{(f)}\longrightarrow\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal F)$, $t/f^a\longmapsto t|_{D_+(f)}\otimes f^{-a}$, where $a\ge0$, $t\in N_a$, and $f^{-a}$ denotes the inverse trivialization of $\mathcal O_X(a)|_{D_+(f)}$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S_0$ and no finiteness hypothesis on $\mathcal F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AG5, lemma-proj-quasi-coherent, isomorphism of the counit; constructions.tex Tag 0B5I, lemma-comparison-proj-quasi-coherent, definition and displayed chart formula; finite degree-one generation supplies the quasi-compact cover required by 0AG5.

proof.text: Choose degree-one algebra generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $S$ over $S_0$. Every positive-degree homogeneous element lies in $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, so this ideal contains $S_+$. By [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open], $X=\bigcup_iD_+(f_i)$ and each chart is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion], $D_+(f_i)\cap D_+(f_j)=D_+(f_if_j)$ is also affine. These charts and intersections are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus the finite cover makes $X$ quasi-compact, and clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] makes it quasi-separated. In particular the degree-one standard opens cover $X$. If $r=0$, then $S_+=0$, $X=\varnothing$, and the empty cover gives the same conclusions.

source.place: Tags 00JP and 01M4 for affine standard opens and their intersections; schemes.tex Tag 01KO (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated), clause (3) implies (1), for the affine-cover criterion; algebra.tex Tag 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact) for affine quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-proj-section-tensor-localization-comparison] with $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ and each $f_i$: it identifies $X_{f_i}$ with $D_+(f_i)$ and $N_{(f_i)}$ with the degree-zero localization of $\bigoplus_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^{\otimes n})$, including the fraction evaluation formula. Since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by Step 1 and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, [lem-sc-p1-invertible-section-localization] says that evaluation is an isomorphism. Thus $\phi_{f_i}:N_{(f_i)}\to\Gamma(D_+(f_i),\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AG5, proof, localized section comparison and application of Tag 01PW(2)

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-proj-section-fraction-naturality], the maps $\phi_g$ for all positive-degree homogeneous $g$ respect every standard-open inclusion. The associated sheaf has sections $N_{(g)}$ and exactly these localization restrictions by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists]. Since the standard opens form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion], these maps define a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear sheaf map $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}:\widetilde N\to\mathcal F$: on any open, restrict a section to its standard-open subcharts, apply $\phi_g$, and glue the compatible results. This also proves the required formula on every $D_+(f)$ with $f\in S_1$, not only on the chosen generators. The source is quasi-coherent by the associated-sheaf statement and the target by hypothesis. Step 2 gives bijectivity on sections of every affine in the cover of Step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-iso-on-affine-cover] makes $\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}$ an isomorphism, including $X=\varnothing$.
